clue.text: Dante's divine work is diffident about Italian sea

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other, so the shy word wraps the sea

parts.note: diffident means shy, or coy
the Med (Mediterranean) is the sea that washes Italy

explanation.surface: A critic says Dante's great poem is curiously bashful about the sea off Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's masterpiece is La Divina Commedia, known in English as the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: It's put down precisely — by Holstein?

indicators.note: by means the cow word stands next to the exact word

parts.note: a Holstein is a breed of dairy cow
pat means precisely, as in knowing something off pat

explanation.surface: A farmer notes that something is placed exactly beside a dairy cow.
explanation.walkthrough: What a cow puts down in the field is the answer, so the definition is a wry one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cow dung is dropped onto the ground by the animal.

clue.text: What's commonest in Lammermoor? A mad role, wild, emotive stuff

parts.note: the letter M appears three times in Lammermoor, more than any but R

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of a mad role are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: In Lucia di Lammermoor the heroine's mad scene is wildly over-the-top opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges A MAD ROLE into ELODRAMA. Lucia di Lammermoor is Donizetti's opera with a famous mad scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodrama is sensational, exaggerated drama designed to stir the emotions.

clue.text: Drank up the store

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily, so drank gives toped

explanation.surface: Someone drank the warehouse dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse or warehouse.

clue.text: Run out — it's recalled in a cricket club's puzzle

indicators.note: in tells us the run-out and the turned word sit inside the cricket club

parts.note: CC is the standard abbreviation for cricket club
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters of it's are read backwards

parts.note: it's gives its letters as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A batsman's dismissal is replayed at the local cricket club.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket scenery is a disguise: 'recalled' sends it's backwards (STI), and the whole run-out group sits inside the club's two Cs, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle in which initial letters of lines spell out a word.

clue.text: Nurse's vocation no end of trouble

indicators.note: no tells us a letter is to be taken away from the vocation word

parts.note: a career is a vocation or profession

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the word trouble

explanation.surface: Nursing is a calling that is never free of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes E, the last letter of 'trouble' picked by 'end of', from CAREER.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after someone sick or disabled, as a nurse does.

clue.text: Tainted source of water will do for seed

parts.note: tainted food has gone off
a spring is a natural source of water

explanation.surface: A polluted spring will do for watering the seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed in the biblical sense means descendants, the same as children.

clue.text: Is miserable type picking up bones?

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking up means the pieces are written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: Is a wretched scavenger picking bones out of the rubbish?
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking up' turns IS + RAT into TAR + SI.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the bones of the ankle and upper foot.

clue.text: Catcall about party involved in swindle degrading event

indicators.note: involved in means the inner group is wrapped inside the swindle

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: about means the cat noise goes round the party

parts.note: a mew is the call of a cat
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A heckler's jeer at a party during a con job makes for a humiliating evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a loss of status or dignity, a humiliating fall.

clue.text: What's excessive about French father over a piece of music?

indicators.note: over in a down entry means the first piece sits above the next
about means the excessive letters go round the French father

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, meaning excessive
pere is French for father

explanation.surface: A French priest asks what's so over the top about a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short, light opera with spoken dialogue.

clue.text: Screen background with initially every source of news

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the word with

parts.note: every can mean all, as in all the people
a newspaper, or paper, is a source of news

explanation.surface: A screen backdrop made up of news cuttings from every source.
explanation.definitionFit: On a computer, the image behind the icons on the desktop is called the wallpaper.

clue.text: Structure includes University discussion group

indicators.note: includes means the structure word holds the university letter inside it

parts.note: form means structure or shape

explanation.surface: A university debating society is housed in a purpose-built building.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting or medium for open discussion, named after the Roman public square.

clue.text: Money expert *: Gold? Had it with gold!

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
had shortens to 'd, as in I'd
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A financial adviser exclaims that a client has struck gold twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold appears twice in two different codes: the chemist's AU and the herald's OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is an accountant who checks the financial records of a company.

clue.text: Gave answer about piano accompanying song

parts.note: re means about or concerning
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a Lied is a German art song, plural Lieder

explanation.surface: A singer responds to questions about the piano part in a song.
explanation.definitionFit: To reply is to give a response, so both phrases describe answering in the past tense.

clue.text: Unhappy ladies want hug? That's about right for some married ones

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the letter for right
unhappy suggests the letters of ladies, want and hug are put out of order

explanation.surface: Miserable women want a cuddle, which suits some wives well enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhappy' mixes up the thirteen letters of the women's words, and 'about' wraps that jumble round the right letter so it lands in the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Women married to one's sons are in-laws by marriage, so they are among the married.

clue.text: Artist drew a lung badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of drew a lung are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: An anatomical artist made a poor drawing of a lung.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthias Grünewald was a German Renaissance painter, famous for the Isenheim Altarpiece.

clue.text: One takes on cases in relation to the estate?

definitions.text: One takes on cases in relation to the estate?

parts.words: One takes on cases in relation to the estate?
parts.note: reads like a probate lawyer, but means a frame that carries luggage on top of an estate car

explanation.definitionFit: A luggage frame fitted on top of an estate car carries suitcases.

clue.text: Glaring gap exposed by noisy type

parts.note: loud colours are glaring or garish
a mouth is an opening or gap, as of a cave

explanation.surface: A gaping opening is revealed by someone shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who talks noisily and tactlessly is called a loudmouth.

clue.text: A college article 'intended upset for university types

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means the word is turned upside down, written bottom to top

parts.note: aimed means intended

explanation.surface: A college publishes an article meant to provoke the dons.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of scholars collectively, the people in universities.

clue.text: Expression of individuality in Paris

parts.note: a French saying that each person has their own taste, the equivalent of 'each to their own'

explanation.definitionFit: The French proverb means everyone to their own taste, so it voices individual preference.

clue.text: Sun, obscured, even invisible

indicators.note: obscured suggests the letters of sun are muddled

parts.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: The sun, hidden by cloud, cannot be seen at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not seen is invisible.

clue.text: Men drifting in Norfolk town exhibiting stupidity

indicators.note: in means the jumbled men are put inside the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, an English county

indicators.note: drifting suggests the letters of men wander out of order

explanation.surface: Men wander about a Norfolk town showing how dim they are.
explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is an English county; its small town of Diss is a crossword regular. 'drifting' scatters the men so that their letters fit inside its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimness is a slowness of mind, a synonym for stupidity.

clue.text: Child never allowed aboard old space-station

indicators.note: aboard means the refusal is placed within the space station

parts.note: Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station, abandoned in 2001
no is the word that refuses permission

explanation.surface: Children were never permitted on the old Soviet space station.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is a person under the age of legal adulthood.

clue.text: Hum some lines, omitting nothing

indicators.note: omitting means a letter for nothing is dropped from the words before it

parts.note: O is the round figure for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Someone hums a few lines but leaves nothing out.
explanation.walkthrough: SOME + LL is SOMELL; 'omitting' drops the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hum is British slang for a bad smell, a stink.

clue.text: Guard, say, left mother in downpour

indicators.note: in means left and mother are put inside the rain

parts.note: a downpour is heavy rain
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A guard leaves his mother standing out in the pouring rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a guard as one example of a railway worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A train guard is one kind of railway employee, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: Very strong, ultimately filthy style of humour

parts.note: iron suggests great strength, as in an iron will

indicators.note: ultimately means the very last letter of the word filthy

explanation.surface: Humour that is very strong ends up rather dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is a mode of humour that says the opposite of what is meant.

clue.text: Article, in the, end, recalled craze

annotationWithheld.why: 'Article, in the, end, recalled craze (5)' as printed: reversing A + IN + AM gives MANIA, but nothing in 'the end' yields AM (the setter may have meant 'morning'); no sound parse for the printed words
annotationWithheld.clue: Article, in the, end, recalled craze

clue.text: Pen something to accompany letter?

definitions.meaning: a pen is a fenced area where animals are kept
an item sent in the same envelope as a letter

explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure is both a fenced-in area and a document placed inside an envelope with a letter.

clue.text: Brought up drink for dog

parts.note: to air a topic is to bring it up for discussion
ale is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone raised the matter of a pint for the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire.

clue.text: Japanese drama character mostly recalled as a crawler

indicators.note: recalled means the drama and the shortened character are each read back to front

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama

indicators.note: mostly means take all but the final letter of the word

parts.note: a type is a character, as in 'an odd type'

explanation.surface: A figure from Japanese theatre is remembered as a grovelling flatterer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TYPE to TYP; 'recalled' reverses NOH + TYP to give PYT + HON.
explanation.definitionFit: A python is a large snake, and snakes crawl along the ground.
